name: Should I touch up isolated spots or repaint the entire wall?

mainEntity.name: Should I touch up isolated spots or repaint the entire wall?

acceptedAnswer.text: Spot touch ups work best for isolated nail holes, minor furniture scuffs, and small drywall dings on flat or matte finishes. If the wall has extensive scuffing across high-traffic paths, significant sun fading, or a satin/semi-gloss sheen, spot painting will likely flash and look patchy. In those situations, rolling the entire wall from corner to corner saves time and delivers a uniform surface without visible brush boundaries.
acceptedAnswer.description: Spot touch ups work well for small dings on flat paint, but high-traffic walls or glossy finishes look much better repainted corner to corner.
